typer-move-tracking-two-passes.value: Move tracking runs in TWO places that must agree. (1) During lowering, src/typer/stmt/dispatch.rs:~402 calls clear_all_moved_for(id) when a bind rebinds an existing name. (2) After each statement is lowered, src/typer/stmt/block.rs calls record_take_moves_in_stmt (src/typer/lower/block.rs), which marks consuming-call args / assignment sources as moved. Pass 2 runs AFTER pass 1, so if it marks the argument of `g is grow(g, x)` as moved it undoes pass 1's revival and rejects the canonical builder idiom. Fix (v133): record_take_moves_in_stmt clears the moved-state of the Bind target (b.def_id) and Assign target (*tid) at the END of handling that statement. Revival stays precise because clearing keys on the TARGET, so `h is grow(g,2)` still tombstones g. Any future move rule must be added to BOTH passes or the invariant breaks silently.

typer-constructor-fallthrough-hole.value: src/typer/expr/construct.rs lower_struct_or_variant used to END with an unconditional Ok(Type::Struct(name)) — so ANY unresolved constructor name fabricated a struct type and compiled+ran (`x is Bogus()` exited 0). Fixed v134: guard on self.structs.contains_key before the fallthrough, else unknown_constructor_error(). That error does (a) a FOREIGN table mapping other languages' prelude spellings to Jinn's (None/Null/Nil->Nothing, Just->Some, Error->Err), then (b) Levenshtein over structs+variant_tags with budget (len/3).clamp(1,3), filtering out mangled `__G_` names. Lesson: any "fall through to a default type" in the typer is a soundness hole — unresolved names must be errors. The Option variant is spelled `Nothing`, NOT `None` (jinn.md was wrong and was corrected).

jinn-surface-conventions.value:
Load-bearing Jinn surface rules, each learned by violating it:
1. `"" + n` is NOT string conversion. The typer deliberately rejects mixed string/int `+` (typer/expr/op.rs). Use `to_string(n)`.
2. Types are GLOBAL and UNQUALIFIED across modules (docs/std.md); functions are qualified. Write `! NetError`, never `! net.NetError` — the parser rejects a dot in a type position.
3. `copy` / `take` / `const` are BINDING modifiers (access-semantics.md §2), not expressions. `copy self` in tail position fails with "Load of undefined variable `copy`". Bind first (`c is copy x`) or write a clone helper.
4. Option's empty variant is `Nothing`, not `None`. Result is `Ok`/`Err`.
5. Errors are values: fallible functions declare `! E` (sugar for `Result of T, E`), raise with `err Variant`, and handle with the quaternary `e ? ok ! nothing !! err` or `match`. Do NOT use `return false` sentinels — that C-ism is what broke std/net.
6. Quaternary arms must agree in type; `log()` returns void, so `r ? log($) !! log('x')` in a value position is a type error.
7. extern `%i8`/`%u8`/`%void` params are C opaque handles — any raw pointer or String is accepted (typer/mod.rs check_extern_arg). Other pointees unify strictly.
8. Empty typed vec: just `vec()` and let inference resolve from a later push. `[] as [T]` is invalid — `as` is only numeric/bool/enum-discriminant/raw-pointer.

test-suite-cost-model-2026-08.value:
Measured on 8-core box. `cargo test --release` = 66s wall / 4m30s CPU. Incremental rebuild after touching src/main.rs = 1.8s (NOT the bottleneck; tests are).
Per-jinnc-invocation cost (2-line program): process startup before any work 22ms, of which ~14ms is dynamic-loading /usr/lib/libLLVM.so.21.1 (157MB) — proven by empty C main linked -lLLVM (14.3ms) vs /bin/true (1.8ms). Frontend+MIR+codegen ~8ms. cc link ~20-50ms. Full compile+link ~85ms.
~1600 tests each fork jinnc => startup alone ~35s CPU.
Suite wall times (--test-threads=8), serial sum ~100s: bulk_tests 19.3s (912 tests, parallel), ownership_fuzz 18.3s (1 proptest, 200 cases, SERIAL), coercion_property 14.0s (6 proptests x64 cases x2 compiles O0+O3), programs_harness 12.2s (1 test looping 87 programs SERIALLY), integration 9.5s (446 tests), doc_examples 7.7s (1 test looping ~50 blocks SERIALLY). Rest <1.8s.
Biggest structural waste: single-#[test] harnesses loop serially, pinning ONE core while cargo runs test binaries one target at a time.
mold/lld NOT installed; ld.gold exists but is SLOWER (54ms vs 14ms) — do not switch linkers.

test-runtime-optimization-2026-08.value:
Test suite sped up 65s -> 40.5s (2019 tests, parity verified against cargo).
What worked (in order of payoff):
1. scripts/test.sh — runs test BINARIES concurrently. `cargo test` runs targets strictly one at a time, so idle cores are the single biggest waste. JOBS defaults to nproc/2, INNER=2 (product ~= nproc).
2. Parallelized single-#[test] corpus harnesses via tests/support/parallel.rs par_map (std::thread::scope, no new deps, order-preserving): programs_harness 7.15->1.85s, doc_examples 3.58->1.31s.
3. Sharded ownership_fuzz's 200-case proptest into 8 x 25-case #[test]s so libtest parallelizes: 9.38->2.56s.
4. tests/support/cases.rs: JINN_PROPTEST_CASES env knob; coercion_property default 64->24 locally, CI + preflight set 64 to keep coverage.
HARDWARE REALITY (do not re-litigate): reference box is 4-core/8-thread i7-8650U @1.9GHz running at 37% freq scaling. nproc=8 overcommits REAL cores. Past ~nproc in-flight compiles total CPU inflates and wall time gets WORSE (measured 8x8 oversubscription: 207s->321s CPU, 58->68s wall). Wall-clock A/B swings 2x from thermal throttling — always re-measure on an idle box, interleave repeats.
Per-compile cost: 16-22ms jinnc startup (mostly mapping 157MB libLLVM.so) + ~8ms compile + 35-50ms cc/ld link = ~90ms. LINK IS THE BIGGEST SINGLE COST -> prefer --emit-hir/--emit-mir assertions over compile-and-run for frontend tests.
Linker swap evaluated and REJECTED: mold/lld not installed; ld.gold measured SLOWER (54ms vs 14ms) than default ld.
PITFALL fixed in runner: basename without the compiler-hash suffix collapses src/lib.rs and src/main.rs test binaries (both named `jinnc`) into ONE log file, silently dropping 309 lib tests and masking their failures. Keep the hash in log filenames. Verified failure detection with deliberate canaries in both a tests/*.rs suite and src/lib.rs.
Docs: docs/testing.md.
